claims.text: The target alloy initially contains a non-equilibrium, metastable solid solution.
Severe plastic deformation generates a high dislocation density in the alloy.
Severe plastic deformation refines the alloy grain structure.
Annealing at 400–550 °C can preserve or enhance the deformation-induced defect density while preventing recrystallization.
Dislocations and refined grains trap solute atoms.
The deformation-induced defect structure accelerates short-circuit diffusion.
The combined effects of solute trapping and short-circuit diffusion delay intermetallic-compound nucleation.
The combined effects of solute trapping and short-circuit diffusion delay intermetallic coarsening.
Delayed intermetallic transformation maintains the integrity of protective oxide layers.
Delayed intermetallic transformation maintains the integrity of passivating layers.
Maintaining protective oxide and passivating layers preserves corrosion resistance relative to the unprocessed metastable alloy.
Maintaining protective oxide and passivating layers preserves high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the unprocessed metastable alloy.
The processed alloy will develop finer and more homogeneously distributed intermetallic precipitates than the baseline.
The processed alloy will exhibit slower intermetallic coarsening at elevated temperatures than the baseline.
The as-cast or conventionally processed baseline undergoes rapid, uncontrolled intermetallic formation at high temperature.
Rapid intermetallic formation in the baseline degrades its protective properties in high-temperature oxidizing environments.
The proposed mechanism and retained resistance are applicable up to approximately 650 °C under inert through low-level oxidizing atmospheres.
Additional mechanisms may govern behavior beyond approximately 650 °C or outside the stated atmospheric range.
